mainTopic: Bad fortune in אב, and the laws of laundering and haircuts in the week of תשעה באב: before and after the fast
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier idea. Since אב is a time of bad fortune and אדר a time of good fortune, a Jew should delay a court case with a non-Jew in אב and try to hold it in אדר. Two short teachings of רב follow, explaining verses in ירמיהו and בראשית. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, which forbids haircuts and laundering in the week of תשעה באב. רב נחמן allows laundering to put clothes away, but רב ששת forbids even that. After a back-and-forth about the Thursday permission, a ברייתא refutes רב נחמן. רבי יוחנן adds that linen, though not subject to the fine-laundering rule, may not be worn that week. רב and שמואל then argue whether the restrictions continue after the fast. A ברייתא seems to refute שמואל, but he answers that תנאים already disagreed about this. רבי יוחנן says all three תנאים learned their views from one פסוק in הושע, and the גמרא begins matching each view to a word in it, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Avoid court cases with a non-Jew in אב; seek them in אדר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws a practical lesson: a Jew should delay a court case against a non-Jew during אב and try to hold it in אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, a Jew who has a court case with a non-Jew should avoid him in אב, when the Jewish people's fortune is weak, and should make himself available in אדר, when their fortune is strong.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the earlier teaching that joy is reduced in אב and increased in אדר, and turns it into practical advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הלכך ('therefore') shows this is a conclusion built on what came before. If אב is a time of bad מזל for Jews and אדר is a time of good מזל, a smart person will time a risky court case to fall in אדר.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; drawing a practical result from a previous teaching
He should slip away from, avoid

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
a Jew who has
a court case with a gentile,
should avoid him in Av,
when his fortune is bad,
and he should make himself available in Adar,
when his fortune is good.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about אב and אדר with practical advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delay a court case with a non-Jew from אב, and try to have it in אדר.

steps.title: A future and a hope: palm trees and linen garments
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, explains in the name of רב that the 'future and hope' in ירמיהו refers to palm trees and linen garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the verse 'To give you a future and a hope,' רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: these are palm trees and linen garments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short teaching from the same chain of רבנן quoted just before, explaining a verse about the exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'future and hope' as things that last a long time and keep giving benefit. Palm trees keep producing for many years, and linen garments last a long time.

phrases.english: "To give you a future and a hope"
Rav Yehuda, son of

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
These are palm trees and linen garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״לָתֵת לָכֶם אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה״, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching added because it comes from the same chain of רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'future and hope' of the verse means long-lasting things: palm trees and linen garments.

steps.title: The smell of יעקב was like a field of apple trees
steps.stepSummary: The same chain explains that the 'field blessed by ה׳' that יצחק smelled was a field of apple trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the verse 'See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that ה׳ has blessed,' רב יהודה son of רב שמואל בר שילת said in the name of רב: like the smell of a field of apple trees.
steps.whatsHappening: A second short teaching from the same chain explains which field יצחק meant when he smelled יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only says 'a field ה׳ blessed' without naming the field. רב fills this in: it was a field of apple trees, known for its sweet smell.

phrases.english: "And he said: See, the smell of my son
is like the smell of a field which the Lord has blessed"
Rav Yehuda, son of

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav:
Like the smell of a field of apple trees.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיֹּאמֶר רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same chain of רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blessed field in the verse was a field of apple trees.
steps.whatToRemember: Steps 2 and 3 are side teachings grouped together because they come from the same chain of רבנן, not because their topics are connected.

steps.title: The משנה: no haircuts or laundering in the week of תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: in the week when תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to do laundry.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the week in which תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the rule it is about to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next steps. The משנה says laundering is forbidden but does not say whether that means only laundering in order to wear, or even laundering to store away.

keyTerms.meaning: The week in which (a day) falls; here שַׁבָּת means 'week'

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבת does not mean the day of שבת. It means the week in which תשעה באב falls.

phrases.english: The week in which the Ninth of Av falls
to be within it,
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the משנה after the side teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the week of תשעה באב, cutting hair and laundering are forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only laundering in order to wear is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the משנה: only laundering in order to wear the clothes is forbidden, while laundering to put them away is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: They only taught this about laundering and wearing, but laundering and putting the clothes away is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains how far the משנה's ban on laundering goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, the problem is wearing freshly washed clothes in a mourning week. Washing them to store for after תשעה באב is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) about; a way of limiting a teaching
And to put aside, to store

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: They only taught
about laundering and wearing,
but to launder and set aside is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's ban reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only laundering in order to wear is forbidden; laundering to store is permitted.

steps.title: רב ששת: even laundering to put away is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת disagrees and says even laundering clothes to put away is forbidden that week.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: Even to launder and put away is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the opposite view from רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ששת, the act of laundering itself is forbidden in the week of תשעה באב, even if the clothes will not be worn until later.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Even to launder and set aside is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְכַבֵּס וּלְהַנִּיחַ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laundering itself is forbidden, even to store the clothes.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof: the launderers of רב's household stopped working
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת supports his view: the launderers of רב's household did not work during that week.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: You can see that this is true, because the launderers of רב's household were idle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings evidence from real life to back up his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If laundering to store were allowed, the launderers could have kept working and set the clothes aside. Since they stopped completely, the act of laundering itself must be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that it is so); introduces a supporting proof
Launderers (people who washed and treated cloth)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Know that this is so,
for the launderers of Rav's household were idle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: תֵּדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב ששת's view in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That even laundering to store is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice in רב's household: the launderers did not work that week.

steps.title: רב המנונא quotes the Thursday permission from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא begins a challenge against רב נחמן by quoting the משנה's rule that on Thursday these things are allowed in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא raised an objection: On Thursday they are permitted, because of the honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא opens a challenge by quoting a line from the משנה. This step only sets up the attack, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows laundering on Thursday of that week for the honor of שבת. רב המנונא is going to ask what kind of laundering this must be, and use the answer against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection:
On Thursday they are permitted,
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attack on רב נחמן (step 5) using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that laundering to store is permitted all week.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source that will be used: the משנה permits laundering on Thursday because of שבת.

steps.title: What honor of שבת is there in wearing clean clothes on Thursday?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא argues that the Thursday permission cannot be about laundering in order to wear, since wearing clothes on Thursday does nothing for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is permitted? If you say laundering and wearing, what honor of שבת is there in that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא asks what the Thursday permission refers to, and rules out the option of laundering in order to wear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing clean clothes on Thursday does not honor שבת. So the משנה must mean laundering to set aside for שבת. That suggests that on other days, even laundering to set aside is forbidden, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? To what does it refer?
If you say; brings up a possible reading in order to reject it

steps.confusionAlert: רב המנונא is not against laundering on Thursday. He is using the Thursday permission to show what the משנה forbids on the other days.

phrases.english: To what does this refer?
If we say it means to launder and to wear,
what honor of Shabbat is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי? אִילֵימָא לְכַבֵּס וְלִלְבּוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds out the challenge set up in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that laundering to set aside is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Thursday permission only makes sense for laundering to set aside for שבת. That means laundering to set aside is forbidden on the other days of the week, which goes against רב נחמן.

steps.title: The Thursday permission must be about laundering to put away
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא finishes his challenge. The Thursday permission must be about laundering to put away, so on other days of the week even that is forbidden, which goes against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must mean laundering to put away. And it is only on Thursday that this is allowed, but the whole rest of the week it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא completes the attack he began in steps 8-9. Since the Thursday permission cannot be about wearing, it must be about putting away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If laundering to put away needed a special Thursday permission, then on the other days of the week it must be forbidden. That is exactly the opposite of רב נחמן, who allowed laundering to put away all week.

keyTerms.meaning: to put away (to store the clothes for later)
here it means 'week', not the day of rest

steps.confusionAlert: In this sugya 'הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ' means 'the whole week', not the day of שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, it must mean laundering to put away.
And it is only on Thursday that it is permitted,
but the whole week it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְהַנִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that laundering to put away is allowed all week
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Thursday permission must be about putting away. That means putting away is forbidden on the other days.

steps.title: The Thursday permission is for someone with only one shirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Thursday permission really is about laundering to wear, in the case of someone who owns only one shirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה means laundering in order to wear, and it is talking about someone who has only one shirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב נחמן. It says the Thursday permission is about wearing after all, but in a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא assumed wearing on Thursday does nothing for שבת. But if a person has only one shirt, he must wash it now so it will be clean for שבת, and he wears it in the meantime. So the Thursday rule fits 'laundering to wear', and רב נחמן's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: really / in truth (introduces a defense of the original reading)
shirt, garment worn next to the body

phrases.english: Really, it means to launder and wear,
and it is when he has only one shirt.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לְכַבֵּס וְלִלְבּוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 8-10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה is about a person with only one shirt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Laundering to wear on Thursday could not help שבת, so the rule must be about putting away.
steps.terutzMaskana: With only one shirt, laundering to wear on Thursday is for שבת's honor, so רב נחמן's reading holds.

steps.title: Support: a one-shirt owner may launder on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the one-shirt case already has special treatment. רבי יוחנן allows such a person to launder on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: someone who has only one shirt may launder it on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing that 'only one shirt' is a known reason for leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering is normally forbidden on חול המועד, yet רבי יוחנן permits it for someone with one shirt. This shows that his need is taken seriously, so it is reasonable for the משנה to allow him to launder on Thursday too.

keyTerms.meaning: the middle days of a festival, when laundering is normally forbidden

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: One who has only one shirt
is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the one-shirt answer of step 11.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about laundering on חול המועד

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the same as רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר, who says the משנה forbids only laundering to wear and allows laundering to put away. This matches רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי בנימין said in the name of רבי אלעזר: the משנה only taught that laundering to wear is forbidden, but laundering to put away is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא who rules exactly like רב נחמן, as extra support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument but a matching opinion. רבי אלעזר also limits the משנה to laundering in order to wear, so רב נחמן is not alone.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (another Amora said the same thing)
they only taught (this case), limiting the rule

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי בִּנְיָמִין אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Binyamin said that Rabbi Elazar said:
They taught it only about laundering and wearing,
but laundering to put away is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא who agrees with רב נחמן after his view was defended.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids laundering even to put away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says laundering before תשעה באב is forbidden even if the clothes are stored until after the fast. It also says Babylonian fine laundering counts like their plain laundering, and linen is not subject to the fine-laundering rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: It is forbidden to launder before תשעה באב, even to put the clothes away until after תשעה באב. Our fine laundering is like their plain laundering. And linen clothes are not included in the rule about fine laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that directly contradicts רב נחמן (and רבי אלעזר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allowed laundering to put away. The ברייתא says explicitly 'even to put away' is forbidden. The extra lines tell us which kinds of laundering count: in Babylonia only fine laundering counts, and linen is left out of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: they challenged (from a ברייתא or משנה)
fine laundering / pressing that makes clothes look bright

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
It is forbidden to launder before the Ninth of Av,
even to put it away until after the Ninth of Av.
And our fine laundering is like their plain laundering.
phrases.notes: 'Ours' means in Babylonia and 'theirs' means in ארץ ישראל. Our plain washing doesn't count as laundering here.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְלֵי פִשְׁתָּן אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּהוּץ.
phrases.english: And linen garments are not subject to the rule of fine laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אָסוּר לְכַבֵּס לִפְנֵי תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב נחמן was defended, a new and stronger source is brought against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן (and רבי אלעזר): laundering to put away is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'even to put away until after תשעה באב' is forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא refutes רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion. רב נחמן's view cannot stand against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is offered, so laundering even to put away is forbidden that week. This matches רב ששת from step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: a refutation; the view has been disproven

steps.whatToRemember: Final result: during the week of תשעה באב, laundering is forbidden even just to put the clothes away, like רב ששת and against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the ברייתא of step 14 refutes רב נחמן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן is refuted. Laundering even to put away is forbidden in the week of תשעה באב.

steps.title: Linen clothes may not be worn during the week of תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that even though linen is not subject to the fine-laundering rule, wearing freshly laundered linen during the week of תשעה באב is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר גיורי sent in the name of רבי יוחנן: even though they said linen clothes are not subject to the fine-laundering rule, it is still forbidden to wear them during the week in which תשעה באב falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the last line of the ברייתא about linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא might seem to make linen fully allowed. רבי יוחנן clarifies that this only means the laundering rule does not apply to it. Wearing it during that week is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: sent (a ruling sent by letter or messenger)

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Giyorei sent in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Although they said

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי פִשְׁתָּן אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּהוּץ,
phrases.english: that linen garments are not subject to the rule of fine laundering,
still, it is forbidden to wear them

phrases.aramaic: בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ.
phrases.english: in the week in which the Ninth of Av falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב יִצְחָק בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the linen line of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Linen is not subject to the laundering rule, but it may not be worn during the week of תשעה באב.

steps.title: רב: the restrictions apply only before the fast
steps.stepSummary: רב says the week's restrictions apply only before תשעה באב. After the fast, laundering is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: they only taught this about the days before תשעה באב, but after it, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: do the week's restrictions continue after the fast? רב says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids these things 'in the week in which תשעה באב falls'. רב reads this as covering only the days leading up to the fast.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: Rav said: They taught this only about before it,
but after it, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the days after תשעה באב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The restrictions apply only before תשעה באב. Afterward, laundering is allowed.

steps.title: שמואל: the restrictions continue after the fast
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees and says that even after תשעה באב, laundering stays forbidden for the rest of that week.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: even after it, it is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the opposite view to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, 'the week in which תשעה באב falls' means the whole week, including the days after the fast.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even after it, it is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחֲרָיו נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laundering stays forbidden for the whole week, even after תשעה באב.

steps.title: A ברייתא about which days of the week are restricted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא to challenge one side of the רב-שמואל argument. It explains that if תשעה באב falls on Sunday, laundering is allowed the whole week before.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: in the week in which תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder, but on Thursday these are allowed in honor of שבת. How so? If it falls on Sunday, it is allowed to launder the whole week before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It starts quoting a ברייתא that goes through the days of the week, and the quote continues in steps 20-22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains how 'the week of תשעה באב' works day by day. When the fast is on Sunday, the week before is not its week, so laundering is allowed. The rest of the ברייתא, still to come, will show whether the days after the fast are included, which is the point רב and שמואל argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunday (the first day of the week)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ —
phrases.english: In the week in which the Ninth of Av falls,
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted in honor of Shabbat.
How so?
If it falls on Sunday,
it is permitted to launder the entire week.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins testing the רב-שמואל argument against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, who forbids laundering even after תשעה באב (the challenge is stated outright in step 23)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's day-by-day breakdown will say that after the fast laundering is permitted (step 20), which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: weekday and Friday cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: if תשעה באב falls Monday through Thursday, laundering is forbidden before it and allowed after it. If it falls on Friday, laundering is allowed on Thursday, and even on Friday afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: If תשעה באב falls on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, laundering is forbidden on the days before it and allowed on the days after it. If it falls on Friday, you may launder on Thursday out of respect for שבת. If you did not launder on Thursday of that week, you may launder on Friday from מנחה time onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in the last step. This is the line that will be used against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'after it, it is permitted.' That says laundering is allowed in the days after תשעה באב, which is exactly רב's view and the opposite of שמואל's. The Friday case adds that respect for שבת can even push laundering onto תשעה באב itself, from the afternoon on.

keyTerms.meaning: Before it (the days before תשעה באב)
After it (the days after תשעה באב)

steps.confusionAlert: In 'בַּחֲמִישִׁי בְּשַׁבָּת' the word שבת means 'the week,' not Saturday. It means Thursday of that week.

phrases.english: If it falls on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday,
phrases.notes: 'It' is תשעה באב. The ברייתא is going through the days of the week.

phrases.english: before it, it is forbidden; after it, it is permitted.
If it falls on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לְכַבֵּס בַּחֲמִישִׁי מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: it is permitted to launder on Thursday, out of respect for שבת.
And if he did not launder on Thursday of that week,
he may launder on Friday
from מנחה time onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשֵּׁנִי בַּשְּׁלִישִׁי בָּרְבִיעִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי, לְפָנָיו — אָסוּר, לְאַחֲרָיו — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל, who forbids laundering even after תשעה באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says that after the fast, laundering is permitted.

steps.title: אביי curses this Friday-afternoon leniency
steps.stepSummary: אביי, or some say רב אחא בר יעקב, cursed this ruling of laundering on Friday afternoon of תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי, and some say רב אחא בר יעקב, cursed this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא for a short side comment. An אמורא strongly disapproves of laundering on תשעה באב afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the ברייתא allows it, אביי sees laundering on תשעה באב itself as disgraceful. This is a reaction to one detail. It does not affect the main question about רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another name for who said it)

phrases.english: אביי cursed over it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, אַהָא.
phrases.english: and some say רב אחא בר יעקב, over this.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the last ruling, laundering on Friday afternoon when that Friday is תשעה באב.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָיֵיט עֲלַהּ אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side comment on the Friday case in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laundering on תשעה באב afternoon is strongly disapproved.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: Torah reading on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes with how many people read from the Torah on תשעה באב, depending on the day of the week. רבי יוסי says it is always three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If תשעה באב falls on Monday or Thursday, three people read, and one of them reads the הפטרה. On Tuesday or Wednesday, one person reads, and that same one reads the הפטרה. רבי יוסי says: three always read, and one of them reads the הפטרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the ברייתא, which turns to Torah reading. This is quoted only to finish the ברייתא before the challenge is stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Monday and Thursday already have a set reading with three people, so it stays that way. On other days, the first view says only one person reads. רבי יוסי says תשעה באב always gets three readers.

keyTerms.meaning: Reads the הפטרה (the portion from the נביאים)

phrases.english: If it falls on Monday or Thursday,
three read, and one reads the הפטרה.
phrases.notes: The one who reads the הפטרה is one of the three.

phrases.english: On Tuesday or Wednesday,
one reads, and one reads the הפטרה.
רבי יוסי says:
Three always read, and one reads the הפטרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי — קוֹרִין שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמַפְטִיר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in steps 19–20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Monday or Thursday three read; on Tuesday or Wednesday one reads. רבי יוסי says three always read.

steps.title: The ברייתא refutes שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the ברייתא is a strong refutation of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא states the challenge outright: the ברייתא contradicts שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'after it, it is permitted,' meaning laundering is fine after תשעה באב. שמואל said it stays forbidden all that week, so he seems to be contradicted by an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation from an authoritative source

phrases.english: A refutation of שמואל!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion of the challenge built from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא permits laundering after the fast, while שמואל forbids it.

steps.title: שמואל answers: it is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the issue is a dispute among תנאים. He brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר forbids laundering only until the fast, but רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbid it beyond that.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can say to you: it is a dispute between תנאים. As it was taught: when תשעה באב falls on שבת, or the day before תשעה באב falls on שבת, a person eats and drinks all he needs and may set a table even like שלמה's feast in his time. Cutting hair and laundering are forbidden from ראש חודש until the fast, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the entire month is forbidden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: it is forbidden only during that week.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends himself. The ברייתא that challenged him follows one opinion, and other תנאים agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר stops the restriction at the fast. רבי יהודה forbids the whole month, which reaches past the fast. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids that whole week, which also includes the days after תשעה באב. So the ברייתא that challenged שמואל is only one view, and שמואל can follow these other תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
That week (the week of תשעה באב)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל is not refuted. He follows רבי יהודה or רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who forbid laundering even after the fast. The ברייתא that challenged him reflects a different view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how an אמורא can survive a challenge from a ברייתא by showing that תנאים themselves disagreed.

phrases.english: שמואל can say to you: it is a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: As it was taught: תשעה באב that falls on שבת,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: and likewise the day before תשעה באב that falls on שבת,
he eats and drinks all he needs,
and puts on his table
even a meal like שלמה's in his time.
And it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder

phrases.aramaic: מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: from ראש חודש until the fast; these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַחֹדֶשׁ כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: the entire month is forbidden.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: it is forbidden only during that week.
phrases.notes: 'That week' includes the days after תשעה באב, which is why this helps שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the challenging ברייתא reflects only one view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the only view, so שמואל is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Other תנאים (רבי יהודה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) forbid laundering even after the fast, and שמואל follows them.

steps.title: A second ברייתא with the same dispute about mourning
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא records the same three opinions about keeping mourning practices from ראש חודש, again showing that some תנאים extend the restrictions past the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another ברייתא teaches: one keeps mourning practices from ראש חודש until the fast, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: the whole month is forbidden. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: it is forbidden only during that week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same dispute. It adds support that שמואל has תנאים behind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא speaks about mourning practices in general, not just haircuts and laundering. The same split shows up: רבי מאיר stops at the fast, while רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reach beyond it, as שמואל does.

phrases.english: And another ברייתא teaches:
And one keeps mourning practices from ראש חודש
until the fast; these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַחֹדֶשׁ כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: the entire month is forbidden.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אָסוּר אֶלָּא אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: it is forbidden only during that week.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: וְנוֹהֵג אֵבֶל מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא that backs up שמואל's answer in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים disagree about whether mourning restrictions continue past תשעה באב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא with the dispute of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל

steps.title: All three opinions come from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל all learned their opinions from the same פסוק: "And I will cause all her joy to cease, her festival, her new month, and her Shabbat."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All three of these תנאים expounded one פסוק, as it is written: "And I will cause all her joy to cease, her festival, her new month, and her Shabbat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us that the three opinions from the earlier ברייתות are not random. They all come from one פסוק, and each תנא reads a different word in it as the key.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we saw three opinions about how long the mourning restrictions last. רבי יוחנן now adds that they share one source in the נביא, where ה׳ says He will stop Israel's joy. The argument is only about which word in the פסוק sets the time period.

keyTerms.meaning: All three of them, here meaning the three תנאים
They expounded, meaning they learned a teaching from the words

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a מחלוקת among תנאים can come from reading the same פסוק in different ways, not from having different sources.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And all three of them expounded one verse,
phrases.notes: "All three" means רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the ברייתא we just saw.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And I will cause all her joy to cease,
her festival, her new month, and her Shabbat."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁלׇשְׁתָּן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the shared scriptural source behind the three opinions brought in Steps 24 and 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three opinions about the length of the mourning restrictions come from one פסוק in הושע.

steps.title: Starting to explain the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to show how each opinion reads the פסוק, starting with the one who says the restrictions last from ראש חודש until the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said the restrictions apply from ראש חודש until the fast...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It names the first opinion, from ראש חודש until the fast, and is about to show which word in the פסוק that opinion relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is only half a sentence. It opens a list that will match each of the three opinions to one word of the פסוק. This first one is the view of רבי מאיר from the earlier ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said, used to point to a specific opinion
The first day of the month, here the start of the month of אב
The fast, here meaning תשעה באב

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished here. The answer to which word this opinion learns from comes in the next line of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית —
phrases.english: The one who said from the New Moon until the fast —

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד הַתַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins applying רבי יוחנן's statement by matching the first opinion to the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces how the opinion of 'from ראש חודש until the fast' is drawn from the פסוק (completed in the next line).
